title: Polynomials and Factorisation: Breaking Expressions Apart

questions.question: What is the degree of the polynomial 5x³ − x + 4?
questions.rationale: The degree is the highest power of the variable, which is 3 (from the term 5x³).

questions.question: How many terms does a trinomial have?
questions.rationale: By the lesson's naming table: monomial (1 term), binomial (2 terms), trinomial (3 terms).

questions.question: Compute 97 × 103 using a difference of squares.
Factorise x² + 5x + 6.
questions.rationale: Two numbers with product 6 and sum 5 are 2 and 3, so x² + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)(x + 3).

questions.question: Factorise 9x² − 25.
questions.rationale: Both terms are squares: (3x)² − (5)², and a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) gives (3x − 5)(3x + 5).

questions.question: Factorise x³ + 3x² + 2x + 6 by grouping.
questions.rationale: Group as x²(x + 3) + 2(x + 3); the bracket (x + 3) is the common factor, leaving (x + 3)(x² + 2).

questions.question: By the factor theorem, (x − a) is a factor of a polynomial p(x) when:
questions.rationale: The factor theorem says (x − a) divides p(x) exactly when p(a) = 0; more generally dividing by (x − a) leaves remainder p(a).

questions.question: Is (x − 1) a factor of p(x) = x³ − 3x + 2?
questions.rationale: p(1) = 1 − 3 + 2 = 0, so (x − 1) is a factor; the full factorisation is (x − 1)²(x + 2).

questions.question: Simplify (x² − 9)/(x² + 7x + 12).
questions.rationale: Factor fully: (x − 3)(x + 3) over (x + 3)(x + 4); cancel the common factor (x + 3), leaving (x − 3)/(x + 4). Only whole factors may be cancelled, never single terms.
